title: Instrumentation-lite mode + adaptive fallback sampler to reduce trace hot-path overhead
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Background: Recent production regressions traced to tracing hot-path allocations and per-request sampling logic have increased request tail latency for high QPS services. Goal: introduce an "instrumentation-lite" capture mode combined with an adaptive fallback sampler that defers expensive operations off the hot path and only performs full trace materialization for candidate spans. This preserves end-to-end observability and tail-based sampling efficacy while reducing allocation, lock contention, and syscall counts in the hot request path.
design_summary: 1) Instrumentation-lite: SDK agents and ingress hooks will emit a compact trace token (4-8 bytes) into outgoing requests and minimal headers for context propagation. No span-objects or full metadata allocations are created on the hot path; only a tiny pre-allocated struct (<= 32 bytes) is touched. 2) Low-cost prefilter: a tiny probabilistic prefilter runs inline using existing cheap signals (status code class, request size, precomputed latency quantile hint). If prefilter marks a request for telemetry, it upgrades by scheduling a background task to enrich the trace with full spans and metadata. 3) Adaptive fallback sampler: histogram-based feedback controller at the aggregator decides which prefiltered requests get materialized for tail-based sampling and long-tail retention. Controller adapts to QPS and keeps memory/IO budget stable. 4) Compatibility: existing tracing headers still supported; fallback to full instrumentation when an environment flag is set (diagnostics mode).
tradeoffs: Pros: reduces hot-path allocations and locks, predictable memory budget, better tail-latency SLO compliance
Cons: slightly delayed availability of full traces for flagged requests, increased complexity in SDK + collector interaction
Mitigations: provide opt-in diagnostic mode, detailed observability for the budget controller, and rollout in stages (beta small fleets)
acceptance_criteria: Inline per-request allocations reduced by >= 65% for instrumented codepath in microbenchmarks
P90 tail latency for our high-QPS frontend decreases by >= 10ms under load test compared to current baseline
No degradation in sampled-trace utility: regression test suite shows >= 95% parity in post-incident root-cause traces for synthetic failures
Collector controller respects configured memory/io budgets and emits alerts when budgets breached
Migration docs and SDK upgrade guides published
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (SDK changes): add instrumentation-lite mode to Python/Go/Node SDKs with identical API compatibility and feature flagging
Phase 2 (ingress): implement prefilter hook in ingress proxy to attach compact trace token for services that cannot upgrade SDK immediately
Phase 3 (collector): implement adaptive histogram controller and background enrich worker capable of materializing deferred spans
Phase 4 (integration): run gradual canary across low-volume services, gather telemetry, tune controller parameters
Phase 5 (rollout): enable by default for hosted runtime in runtime-1.22 if metrics meet thresholds
benchmarks_and_metrics: Microbench harness: bench/tracing/inline_allocs_test (see PR) measures allocations/op and CPU ns/op
Targets: allocations/op from 240 -> <= 80 on hot path, CPU ns/op reduction >= 25%
Production signals to monitor: p95/p99 request latency, tracer dropped-span-rate, collector-enrichment-queue-length, sampled-trace-coverage
Dashboards: observability/perf/instrumentation-lite (Grafana) and alerts in PagerDuty when enrichment queue > 2k
runbook_notes: If enrichment queue backs up: temporarily raise enrichment-worker replica count and lower prefilter threshold
If sampled trace utility drops: revert SDK flag for that service and open postmortem with SDK/collector owners
Emergency-off: a runtime feature-flag toggle disables instrumentation-lite globally (RBAC: platform-admin)
